title: Synergistic Privacy Architecture
definition: A privacy architecture that leverages directory-level visibility, plausible deniability, and capability-based access to enhance data security and user control.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a digital lockbox where only certain people have the keys to specific compartments. This is a privacy architecture that lets users control who sees their data, even when it's shared across multiple systems.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: This architecture combines directory-level visibility, plausible deniability, and capability-based access to provide users with more control over their data. It allows for selective sharing while maintaining privacy and security.
difficulty_levels.expert: This privacy architecture builds upon the principles of need-to-know and least privilege. It enables users to control access to their data at a granular level, enhancing security and privacy. This architecture also supports interoperability and scalability, making it suitable for decentralized systems like Atlas and CADMIES.

extra_fields.insight: The synergistic privacy architecture presented in the Atlas and CADMIES systems offers a balanced approach to data security and user control, combining directory-level visibility, plausible deniability, and capability-based access.
